items.headline: Democrats win control of the House and Senate
items.summary: Democrats won majorities in both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, a major rebuke to President Trump. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer spoke after his party clinched the Senate majority.

items.headline: Talarico wins Texas Senate race over Paxton
items.summary: Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton for the U.S. Senate in Texas, according to an AP race call. TIME called it a major upset in a state Democrats had not won statewide in decades.

items.headline: Troy Jackson unseats Susan Collins in Maine
items.summary: Democrat Troy Jackson won Maine's U.S. Senate seat, defeating longtime Republican Sen. Susan Collins. Collins conceded the race.

items.headline: El-Sayed holds Michigan Senate seat for Democrats
items.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's open Senate race, days after Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Rogers. El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate.

items.headline: Annie Andrews flips South Carolina Senate seat
items.summary: Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina. The win flipped the seat to Democrats in what TIME called a stunning upset.

items.headline: Amy Acton defeats Vivek Ramaswamy for Ohio governor
items.summary: Democrat Amy Acton won Ohio's governor's race over Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, according to an AP race call. Acton led 50.8% to 45.9% with most votes counted.

items.headline: Trump blames Republican candidates for midterm losses
items.summary: President Trump said Democrats 'did a good job' and blamed Republican candidates for the party's defeats. He also criticized GOP figures and Fox News after the results.

items.headline: Voters decide abortion, redistricting and voting measures
items.summary: Voters in several states decided 145 ballot measures, including on abortion rights, congressional maps and voter ID. Missouri voters rejected a Republican-drawn congressional map, and Virginia approved an abortion-rights amendment.

items.headline: U.S. strikes Iranian targets after Netanyahu pressed for action
items.summary: The United States carried out new strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz, days after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly pressed President Trump for more strikes. A U.S. official described them as a response to Iranian missile fire at U.S. forces.

items.headline: China's expanding mangroves draw more bird species
items.summary: China's restored mangrove forests have spread across large stretches of coastline. Researchers found the expanding forests are attracting a growing number of bird species.

digest.overview:
Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday's midterms, a sharp rebuke to President Trump, putting Hakeem Jeffries on course to become the first Black speaker. Democrats flipped Senate seats in Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton, and in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Iowa, Kansas and South Carolina, while Abdul El-Sayed held Michigan. Mississippi and Alaska remained too close to call, along with dozens of House races. Democrats also flipped governorships in Texas, Ohio, Georgia and Iowa. Missouri voters rejected abortion restrictions and a Republican congressional map, and Virginia approved an abortion-rights amendment. Trump said he would accept the results, blamed Republican candidates and vowed to veto freely. The Supreme Court refused a Justice Department request to set aside about 20,000 California mail ballots.

Abroad, U.S. strikes hit Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's parliament speaker warned of a "new battlefield" as Qatari mediators carried a revised proposal to Tehran. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it downed two U.S. drones. Russia struck Ukraine's power grid with 289 drones and 17 ballistic missiles, knocking three thermal plants offline, and the toll from an attack on an aid site in Zaporizhzhia region rose past 30; peace talks are set for Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11. North Korea fired another projectile on Wednesday, and Kim Yo Jong ruled out talks with Washington for now. Israel reportedly moved to fully close Gaza's Rafah crossing, and Yemen's Houthis advanced to within 50 miles of Aden. Spain's transport minister resigned over a train crash that killed 69. The COP31 climate summit opens Nov. 9 in Antalya, Turkey.

home.overview:
There were no NBA games on Election Day, and the league returns with 14 tonight, led by 7-1 Philadelphia at 6-1 Detroit and Cleveland's visit to Oklahoma City two days after Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 43 points beat the Cavaliers. Draymond Green was ejected for the first time this season after tackling Phoenix's Maluach in Monday's Warriors win. In the NFL, Baltimore signed quarterback Kedon Slovis with Lamar Jackson headed to injured reserve before hosting Jacksonville on Thursday night, Atlanta's James Pearce Jr. was reinstated from an eight-game suspension, and the trade deadline is Nov. 10. Baseball's offseason is heating up: MLB proposed delaying a salary cap in labor talks, Seattle hired Cubs executive Jason Kanzler as manager, and award finalists were announced.

In the Champions League, PSG won 6–0 at Villarreal to stay perfect, Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3–0, Bayern won 2–0 at Atlético and Manchester United edged Roma 3–2, with Real Madrid, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City all away tonight. Birmingham beat Millwall 3–0 to climb to second in the Championship as leaders Middlesbrough visit Wrexham, and MLS closes its regular season on Decision Day Saturday. In the KBO, KT Wiz held off Samsung 8–7 in Game 1 of the Korean Series, with Game 2 played Wednesday night in Suwon.

brief: KT Wiz beat Samsung 8–7 in Game 1 of the Korean Series in Suwon, holding on after Samsung cut an eight-run deficit to one.
Home runs from Ahn Hyun-min, Han Seung-taek and Kim Hyun-soo powered KT, and closer Park Yeong-hyun struck out the last three batters for the save.
Game 2 in Suwon matched KT's Ko Young-pyo against Samsung's Chris Paddack, who started on short rest.
The series moves to Daegu for Games 3–5 from Nov. 6, with Games 6 and 7 in Suwon on Nov. 10–11 if needed.
The late pitcher Choi Dong-won was named a Korean 'Sports Hero'.
